title: Rate Adequacy & Pricing Factor Assessment
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/01 - Rate Adequacy & Pricing Factor Assessment.md
goal: Determine if current premiums accurately reflect underlying risk and costs, and identify whether pricing factors (e.g., driver age, vehicle type, region) are appropriately weighted.
dataRequired: Historical claims data (loss frequency, loss severity, payouts)
Premium and exposure data (written premium, earned premium, in-force policies)
Key rating attributes (driver demographics, driving history, vehicle types, territories)
Competitor rate filings or market benchmarking data
External cost drivers (medical inflation, parts inflation, legal environment)
improve: Conduct regular (e.g., quarterly or annual) pricing reviews to stay ahead of claim cost trends.
Use advanced predictive analytics to refine rating models and capture emerging risk patterns.
Monitor competitor filings and benchmark data to maintain competitive positioning.
Collaborate closely with underwriting and claims departments to gather insights on evolving risks.
Maintain clear documentation and rationale for rate changes to satisfy regulatory requirements.

formulas.output: Loss Ratio
formulas.source: Loss Ratio = (Incurred Losses + Loss Adjustment Expenses) / Earned Premium. Perform this calculation for each relevant rating segment (e.g., age group, territory).

Benchmark against competitors to ensure rates and offerings remain competitive in the market.

formulas.output: Calculate the UM/UIM segment loss ratio using Loss Ratio
formulas.source: Calculate the UM/UIM segment loss ratio using Loss Ratio = (UM/UIM Incurred Losses + Loss Adjustment Expenses) / Earned Premium for UM/UIM. Determine if the segment is profitable, breaking even, or underpriced.

title: GAP Insurance Performance Evaluation
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/03 - GAP Insurance Performance Evaluation.md

Conduct regular market benchmarking to maintain a competitive edge and align with evolving industry practices.

formulas.output: Determine the GAP-specific loss ratio using Loss Ratio
formulas.source: Determine the GAP-specific loss ratio using Loss Ratio = (Incurred GAP Losses + Loss Adjustment Expenses) / Earned Premium. Evaluate whether the loss ratio meets target profitability levels.

Partner with rental agencies or repair shops to control costs and speed up turnaround times.
Educate policyholders on coverage parameters to reduce misunderstandings and improve satisfaction.

title: Glass Coverage & Zero-Deductible Claim Impact
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/05 - Glass Coverage & Zero-Deductible Claim Impact.md

Adjust pricing or deductibles for glass coverage to align with actual loss costs and market conditions.

Monitor state regulations closely to ensure compliance while optimizing product offerings and profitability.

title: Defensive Driving Discount Efficacy
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/06 - Defensive Driving Discount Efficacy.md
goal: Evaluate the impact of defensive driving discounts on loss experience and retention, and determine if this discount effectively rewards safer drivers or if it results in adverse selection.

Refine discount amounts or eligibility criteria based on actual observed risk improvements post-training.
Promote the discount through targeted marketing to attract genuinely safety-conscious drivers.
Work with recognized defensive driving course providers to ensure consistent quality and to gather post-course performance data.

title: Territorial Rating Factor Fine-Tuning
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/07 - Territorial Rating Factor Fine-Tuning.md

Collaborate with local authorities or other data providers to track changes in crime rates, traffic patterns, or road improvements.
Maintain open communication with regulators to ensure territorial rate changes comply with filing requirements and do not raise unfair discrimination concerns.

title: Pay-Per-Mile Insurance Adoption & Loss Results
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/08 - Pay-Per-Mile Insurance Adoption & Loss Results.md
goal: Evaluate the adoption rate, usage patterns, and profitability of pay-per-mile insurance policies to determine if mileage-based pricing accurately reflects risk and fosters sustainable growth.

improve: Refine mileage-based rate tiers to better match usage segments and reduce adverse selection.
Introduce or enhance telematics solutions that more accurately capture driving patterns.

formulas.output: Calculate the adoption rate by using Adoption Rate
formulas.source: Calculate the adoption rate by using Adoption Rate = (Number of Pay-Per-Mile Policies / Total Policies) x 100. Compare this rate over time to understand growth trends.

formulas.output: Calculate a pay-per-mile loss ratio using Loss Ratio
formulas.source: Calculate a pay-per-mile loss ratio using Loss Ratio = (Incurred Losses + Loss Adjustment Expenses) / Earned Premium for pay-per-mile policies. Compare against traditional auto policies to gauge profitability differences.

title: Non-Owned Auto Coverage & Borrowed Vehicle Liabilities Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/09 - Non-Owned Auto Coverage & Borrowed Vehicle Liabilities.md
goal: Evaluate the exposure, claim frequency, and severity of non-owned auto (borrowed or rented vehicle) coverage to ensure appropriate underwriting, pricing, and liability protection.

formulas.output: Calculate the non-owned auto coverage loss ratio using Loss Ratio
formulas.source: Calculate the non-owned auto coverage loss ratio using Loss Ratio = (Incurred Losses + LAE for Non-Owned Auto) / Earned Premium for Non-Owned Auto. Compare these results to standard auto coverage to identify any abnormal patterns.

title: Roadside Assistance Utilization & Cost Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/10 - Roadside Assistance Utilization & Cost Analysis.md
goal: Determine how often policyholders use roadside assistance benefits, evaluate the cost implications of these services, and identify opportunities to optimize pricing and service delivery.
dataRequired: Policy-level data showing who has elected roadside assistance coverage
Historical roadside assistance usage records (frequency, type of service, provider details)
Costs associated with each service call, including towing, on-site repairs, or other services

Refine underwriting criteria for roadside assistance to limit coverage for high-frequency claimants or older vehicles in poor condition.

Periodically review and update coverage terms, such as maximum towing distance, to align with actual usage and cost trends.

formulas.source: Roadside Assistance Frequency = (Number of Roadside Assistance Calls / Number of Policies with Coverage) x 100. Compare across different segments (e.g., vehicle age, driver age, location) to pinpoint high-usage groups.

title: License Points Surcharge Program Evaluation
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/11 - License Points Surcharge Program Evaluation.md
goal: Assess the effectiveness of the license points surcharge program in reflecting driver risk and maintaining profitability, while evaluating the impact on policyholder behavior and retention.

improve: Introduce driver education programs or discounts that encourage improved driving behaviors, potentially reducing points.

formulas.output: Determine the surcharge program loss ratio by applying Loss Ratio
formulas.source: Determine the surcharge program loss ratio by applying Loss Ratio = (Incurred Losses + Loss Adjustment Expenses) / Earned Premium for surcharged drivers. Compare to non-surcharged drivers to identify whether the surcharge appropriately offsets higher risk.

title: Accident Forgiveness Program Profitability Assessment
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/12 - Accident Forgiveness Program Profitability Assessment.md

improve: Refine eligibility criteria for accident forgiveness to ensure it targets safer drivers and prevents abuse.
Adjust premium contributions or surcharges to offset the financial impact of forgiven claims.

formulas.output: Assess overall loss ratio by using Loss Ratio
variables: Earned Premium for accident forgiveness policies

sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/13 - Telematics & Usage-Based Insurance Performance.md

title: Premium Leakage & Under-Reported Exposure Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/14 - Premium Leakage & Under-Reported Exposure Analysis.md
goal: Identify areas where policyholders or agents may under-report driver information, vehicle usage, or other risk factors leading to inadequate premium collection, and determine strategies to recapture lost revenue and align premiums with actual exposure.
dataRequired: Policy information detailing driver counts, vehicle usage (personal, commercial, rideshare), and annual mileage
Claims data segmented by discrepancies in reported vs. actual exposure (e.g., undisclosed drivers, misrepresented garaging address)
Third-party data sources (DMV records, credit checks, telematics, vehicle registration databases)
Audit or inspection reports highlighting inconsistencies between reported and actual exposure
Industry or competitor benchmarks on typical leakage rates and detection methods
improve: Implement automated data cross-checks, pulling from public or private databases (e.g., driver’s license records, telematics).
Strengthen agent training and incentives to ensure thorough risk disclosure and reduce intentional misrepresentation.
Conduct periodic audits or inspections of policies flagged for potential under-reporting based on predictive analytics.
Introduce policyholder self-service tools allowing easy updates of vehicle usage or driver information, reducing accidental misreporting.

formulas.output: Calculate the frequency of discrepancies by using Discrepancy Rate
variables: Number of Policies with Under-Reported Exposures
formulas.source: Calculate the frequency of discrepancies by using Discrepancy Rate = (Number of Policies with Under-Reported Exposures / Total Policies) x 100. Categorize discrepancies by type (e.g., unreported drivers, incorrect mileage, false address).

title: Residual Market & Assigned Risk Pool Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/15 - Residual Market & Assigned Risk Pool Analysis.md

Claims data (frequency, severity, incurred losses, loss adjustment expenses) for these high-risk segments

Collaborate with regulators to align assigned risk rates and policy structures with actual loss experience.
Continuously monitor the size and performance of the assigned risk segment and make data-driven adjustments to underwriting and pricing practices.

formulas.output: Determine the loss ratio for assigned risk policies using Loss Ratio
formulas.source: Determine the loss ratio for assigned risk policies using Loss Ratio = (Incurred Losses + LAE) / Earned Premium. Assess whether the pool’s profitability (or lack thereof) aligns with internal targets and industry norms.

title: SR-22 & High-Risk Driver Segment Performance

Implement tiered pricing or phased renewal approaches to reward proven risk improvement among SR-22/high-risk customers.

formulas.output: Determine segment-level loss ratios using Loss Ratio
formulas.source: Determine segment-level loss ratios using Loss Ratio = (Incurred Losses + LAE) / Earned Premium. Assess whether SR-22/high-risk premiums align with actual claims experience and profitability goals.

Monitor competitor strategies to maintain a competitive yet profitable presence in the non-standard auto market.

title: Claims Frequency & Severity Analysis
sourcePath: data/analysis-library/auto-insurance/22 - Claims Frequency & Severity Analysis.md
goal: Measure how often claims occur (frequency) and how costly they are on average (severity), in order to identify trends, evaluate risk, and guide pricing and underwriting decisions.
dataRequired: Historical claims data (dates, causes, incurred amounts)
Exposure and premium data (written premium, earned premium, policy counts)
Claim payment details (reserves, paid amounts, allocated loss adjustment expenses)
External data on inflation, repair costs, or legal environment affecting claims
Demographic and vehicle-specific details for segmentation (age, vehicle model, location)
improve: Implement predictive analytics to identify early indicators of rising claim frequency or severity.
Adjust underwriting criteria or pricing models to reflect identified risk factors more accurately.
Work with preferred repair networks or negotiate favorable rates to manage repair costs and reduce severity.
Continuously monitor external factors (economic, legal, technological) and update strategies accordingly.

formulas.output: Calculate claim frequency by using Frequency
formulas.source: Calculate claim frequency by using Frequency = (Number of Claims / Number of Exposures) x 100. Break down by relevant segments such as driver age, coverage type, or region.

formulas.output: Compute claim severity by using Severity
formulas.source: Compute claim severity by using Severity = (Total Incurred Losses / Number of Claims). Compare severity across segments to spot unusually high-cost categories.

title: Claim Settlement Speed

Cycle time metrics for each stage of the claims process (e.g., investigation, documentation, approval)
Complexity indicators (type of damage, number of parties involved)
